# Claim comparison: draft against brief

Draft: `draft.md` (heading plus four paragraphs, no byline). Material: `brief.md` only. `notes.md` was not supplied, so the brief is the entire material. Source and target are both Swedish. Nothing is translated, so the translation check has nothing to assess.

## 1. Claim accounting

### C1. Headline
- **Draft:** "Norrmyra bibliotek inför söndagsöppet från 1 november"
- **Source:** §6: "från och med söndag 1 november 2026 har Norrmyra bibliotek öppet på söndagar klockan 11–15." §1: "**Ämne:** Norrmyra biblioteks nya söndagsöppettider." §12: "Varför inför biblioteket söndagsöppet nu?" §7.6: "varför biblioteket inför söndagsöppet."
- **Differences:**
  - *Thing and subject:* the same library and the same Sunday opening.
  - *Verb:* "inför" (introduces) is the brief's own verb (§7.6, §12). The novelty it implies rests on "nya söndagsöppettider" (§1). It says nothing about the unconfirmed "första gången på tio år".
  - *Time:* the headline leaves out the year. The lead's first sentence gives it ("2026"), so the release as a whole keeps the time scope.
  - *Direction test:* I can find no case compatible with the brief in which the library has Sunday opening from 1 November 2026 but is not introducing it. The brief calls the opening hours "nya" (new). I can find no case in the other direction either.
- **Pronouns:** none.
- **Verdict:** supported.

### C2. Lead
- **Draft:** "Från och med söndag 1 november 2026 har Norrmyra bibliotek öppet på söndagar klockan 11–15."
- **Source:** §6: "från och med söndag 1 november 2026 har Norrmyra bibliotek öppet på söndagar klockan 11–15."
- **Differences:** none. Subject, date, day, hours and modality are all identical. The calendar confirms that 1 November 2026 falls on a Sunday.
- **Duration:** the brief does not settle whether the Sunday opening is permanent, a trial or seasonal (§12: "Gäller söndagsöppet tills vidare, under en försöksperiod eller under en viss säsong?"). The draft uses the same wording as the brief and adds no duration. Both statements are true in a trial-period case and in a permanent case, so the draft asserts nothing the brief does not.
- **Pronouns:** none.
- **Verdict:** supported. See also note N1.

### C3. Quotation and attribution
- **Draft:** "”Söndagen är familjernas dag, och nu kan de tillbringa den med böcker”, säger Karin Ek, bibliotekschef på Norrmyra bibliotek."
- **Source:**
  - §7.3: "Karin Ek, bibliotekschef: ”Söndagen är familjernas dag, och nu kan de tillbringa den med böcker.” Anteckningarna innehåller bara det här citatet"
  - §12: "Karin Ek, bibliotekschef: citatet och minnet om att biblioteket inte har haft söndagsöppet på tio år."
  - §6: "Uppgiften kommer från bibliotekschefens minne"
  - §7 (one-sentence summary): "bibliotekschefen Karin Ek menar att söndagen är familjernas dag"
- **Wording:** the draft reproduces the quotation word for word. The only change is the full stop dropped before the speech tag, which is ordinary punctuation. No repair was made, so no meaning, stance, certainty or distinctive wording has changed.
- **Speaker and role:** "bibliotekschef" is given in the brief. The addition "på Norrmyra bibliotek" is settled by context: the definite "bibliotekschefens" and "bibliotekschefen" refer to the sending library, and §2 names that library as Norrmyra bibliotek. The brief contains nothing about a head librarian of any other library.
- **Speech verb:** "säger" matches the brief's use of "citatet", given in quotation marks as Karin Ek's.
- **Pronouns inside the quotation (carried over verbatim):**
  - "de": third person plural. Its referent is "familjernas" (the families). It conveys no natural gender and no number beyond plural, the same as in the source.
  - "den": third person singular, grammatical common gender (utrum), referring to "Söndagen". It is not a natural-gender assertion.
  - The brief carries both pronouns, so neither adds person, number or gender information.
- **Time:** the quotation's "nu" (now) stays as the speaker's word. Placed after the lead, it reads as referring to the new Sunday opening, which is the brief's own use of the quotation (§7.3: "det står direkt efter ingressen").
- **Verdict:** supported. See also note N2.

### C4. Contact
- **Draft:** "För frågor, kontakta Karin Ek, bibliotekschef, telefon 0000-00 00 00, e-post karin.ek@example.se."
- **Source:** §7.8: "**Kontakt:** Karin Ek, bibliotekschef, 0000-00 00 00, karin.ek@example.se." §10: "vet vem som svarar på frågor" (suggested).
- **Differences:** the labels "telefon" and "e-post" name the two contact channels the brief lists. Their formats settle which is which. "För frågor" states the ordinary function of a press contact, which the brief itself assigns (§10). Nothing is added about availability or hours.
- **Pronouns:** none.
- **Verdict:** supported.

### C5. Boilerplate
- **Draft:** "Norrmyra bibliotek är ett kommunalt bibliotek i Norrmyra."
- **Source:** §7.9: "**Om Norrmyra bibliotek:** ett kommunalt bibliotek i Norrmyra." §2: "Norrmyra bibliotek, ett kommunalt bibliotek i den påhittade orten Norrmyra."
- **Differences:** none. The word "påhittade" (invented) describes the evaluation setting given in the brief (§ intro, "allt påhittat för en utvärdering"). It is not a fact the release is meant to assert. The commissioned genre presents Norrmyra as the place.
- **Pronouns:** none.
- **Verdict:** supported.

### Material the draft leaves out, correctly
- **"Första gången på tio år" ("first time in ten years"):** left out. The brief allows it only if confirmed (§8: "Den tas med bara om den bekräftas"), and it has not been confirmed.
- **The library's two beliefs** (that many families with children will come, and that it will become the town's natural meeting place): left out as facts, as §8 requires. The quotation carries the message, as the brief suggests.
- **Other opening hours, address, services on Sundays, reason, decision or funding, attachments:** all missing from the material (§12 open questions), and none is invented.
- **Second quotation:** none is invented (§7.5: "inget citat skrivs för att fylla platsen").

## 2. Findings

### Source-support findings
None. Every factual and attributed claim in the headline, lead, quotation, contact line and boilerplate rests on a quoted passage in the brief. The one-directional or two-directional tests found no case, compatible with the brief, in which the draft's statement holds and the brief's fails, or the reverse.

### Translation findings
None. There is no translation: both source and target are Swedish, and the quotation is reproduced verbatim.

## 3. Notes

These are editorial questions or matters outside source support. None is a defect in what the draft says.

- **N1. Duration of the Sunday opening.** The brief suggests the lead should state whether the Sunday opening is "tills vidare eller under en period, så att ingen tror något annat". It records that the information is missing (§7.2, §12). The draft rightly does not guess. Once the library answers, adding the duration to the lead would close this gap.
- **N2. Status of the quotation.** The brief presents the quotation as Karin Ek's words, in quotation marks, taken from `notes.md`. That file was not supplied, so this comparison cannot tell whether the words were recorded verbatim or reconstructed in notes. Nothing here verifies quote approval.
- **N3. Length.** The draft runs to about 60 words, against the brief's provisional suggestion of 200–350 words. That suggestion is not a binding limit (§1 "[MISSING …] [SUGGESTED …]"). The shortfall reflects missing material, not something missing from the text. The material that would close the gap is listed in the brief's open questions (§12): duration, services on Sundays, reason or decision, other opening hours, address, and confirmation of the ten-year claim.

## 4. Completion status

The comparison is complete. All five draft passages (headline, lead, quotation with attribution, contact, boilerplate) were checked against the brief. There are no unresolved source-support or translation findings. The three notes (N1–N3) are editorial questions that depend on material the brief lists as missing, not defects in the draft.
